messages:
maya (ml): quick sync — ran a prefilling-priority experiment on the new 13B quant build (gptq-4, group=128). summary: p99 down ~22%, p50 ~15% faster, small quality shift on reasoning checks. artifacts: s3://runs/1743219876/artifacts

anil (infra): nice. which quant pipeline + exact cmd? and was KV-cache warmup applied?

maya (ml): used gptq conversion with bits=4, group=128. warmup: 2-step prefix warmup (3k tokens) to populate KV cache. command (run on canary):

```
python run_infer.py --model s3://models/13b-float32 --convert-to gptq --bits 4 --group-size 128 
# deploy: infra/canary/deploy_prefill_toggle=true
```

less verbose: deployed as canary on ded-13b-quant-ops.

tess (research): what eval sets did you use for the "reasoning checks"? small % change could be noise.

maya (ml): ran GSM8K (eval split), MATH-sampled subset, and a 2k prompt slice from our prod-synthetic cohort (paraphrase-heavy). numbers (baseline float32 vs q4+prefill-priority):

- baseline float32: p99=210ms, p50=48ms, ppl(test)=12.50, gsm8k acc=72.1%
- q4 prefill-priority: p99=164ms (-22%), p50=41ms (-15%), ppl=12.70 (+1.6%), gsm8k acc=71.1% (-1.4%)

kai (product): so latency win but small accuracy loss on GSM8K. any per-problem regression clusters?

maya (ml): eyeballing errors — more multi-step arithmetic dropouts, particularly problems needing maintaining long intermediate state. short Q/A unaffected.

anil (infra): curious about tail under concurrency. what was load during benchmark?

maya (ml): load: 500 concurrent synthetic sessions, avg seq len 140 tokens. script used:

```
loadtest --concurrency 500 --rps 2000 --seq-len-dist "p(80)=120,p(20)=380" --endpoint /v1/generate
```

ops-bot: canary deploy recorded: ded-13b-quant-ops -> 2024-05-03T14:12:08Z (rev q4-g128-20240503) :white_check_mark:

anil (infra): can we isolate whether the regression is from quantization vs prefill-priority scheduling? run these arms: (A) q4 but no prefill-priority, (B) float32 + prefill-priority, (C) q4 + prefill-priority (already ran). that should separate scheduling from numeric error.

tess (research): agreed. also run per-step NLL time-series on GSM8K traces — if NLL diverges early in prefix vs late step, that hints at cache/prefill interaction.

maya (ml): good point. I'll queue 3 arms; quick plan: 5k examples each, capture per-token NLL and top-k overlap with baseline. acceptance heuristic: rollback if >1.5% absolute drop in gsm8k acc OR >2.5% relative ppl increase on eval.

kai (product): fine, but also collect user-simulated end-to-end latency (95/99) — product can tolerate slight quality dip if overall UX improved and we can mitigated via targeted fallbacks.

manual note for ops: add a canary fallback policy: if user-critical route (routes: /chat/assist) sees >0.8% error spike, auto-fallback to float32 pool.

anil (infra): I'll provision a no-prefill q4 pool and a float32 prefill-priority pool for the A/B. estimate extra GPUs: 4 gpus each for short run.

maya (ml): started A/B job: job id ab-1743219876-1. logs to s3://runs/1743219876/ab. expected finish ~3h. will post interim NLL diffs.

tess (research): please include per-category buckets (arithmetic, multi-hop, commonsense) and calibration metrics (confidence vs accuracy). also include sampling seed control — we want deterministic comparators.

maya (ml): using fixed seeds + same sampling params. one more check: I saw occasional token-level hallucinations under q4 when prefill is aggressive; will add a small early-exit safety gate in the prefill scheduler (if top1 probability < 0.02 at token t, fall back to conservative prefill).

kai (product): thanks. timeline?

maya (ml): interim results in ~2.5h, full run ~3h. if regressions persist, next steps: try group-size 64 or switch to GPTQ-per-channel variant.

anil (infra): ping me when interim logs are up, I'll run tail-latency stress with real-user traces.

tess (research): if we can keep gsm8k acc drop <0.6% and p99 < -18% we can consider gradual rollout to low-risk tenants.

maya (ml): noted. posting interim snapshot in thread when available. :hourglass:
